subject: Throughput stitch & invoice mitigation plan for Friday spike
message_1_subject: Urgent: Friday traffic spike — request for immediate uplift and credit
message_1_body:
Hi Jasmine,

Quick heads up — we just saw a ~4.5x spike in inference traffic for a subset of routes starting late yesterday and it looks like it's going to continue through Friday due to an unplanned push from our QA cluster. We’re already throttled on the current commit. Can Redwood provide an emergency uplift for Friday (throughput headroom approximately +3x for 24 hours) and advise on how the overage will be invoiced?

Two asks from our side: 1) can you push immediate temporary capacity so our users aren’t impacted, and 2) is there a path to have part of this overrun offset as a one-time credit given this was an internal rollout bug on our side and we’re a mid-commit customer? We can share the internal postmortem after the fact.

We need a quick answer and ETA for uplift. Attached is the traffic dump and a short usage CSV.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Sr. Engineering Manager, Clearway AI
engineering@clearway.ai

Attachment(s): clearway_traffic_report.pdf; usage_snapshot_20261103.csv
message_2_subject: Re: Urgent: Friday traffic spike — request for immediate uplift and credit
message_2_body:
Hi Maya — thanks for the quick flag and for sending the files.

We can absolutely stand up temporary headroom immediately. Options and tradeoffs below — pick what works best and I’ll execute: 

1) Instant burst top-up (recommended for immediate protection): we add +3x capacity on your existing routes for 24 hours. This is billed as PAYG at our overrun rate; we can prorate to the hour. ETA: ~15 minutes to apply.

2) Temporary uplift with invoice smoothing: we apply the capacity now and massage the overrun across this month’s invoice so the spike is spread (no change to unit pricing). This requires a quick procurement acknowledgement from Ethan but we can do same day.

3) Partial courtesy credit (exception): I can request a one-time goodwill credit to offset up to 20% of the overage if approved by Sales Leadership and Finance. This is discretionary and tied to a short write-up you mentioned (postmortem).

If you’re interested in a longer-term fix, we can propose a short-term committed uplift (30–90 days) at a blended rate that will lower per-token cost vs PAYG for this window. If you’d like to discuss conversion to a reserved increment, we can model that.

Next steps I propose: confirm which option (1/2/3 or combo), confirm exact routes (send route IDs) and accept the temporary uplift. If you want the credit path, I’ll route an internal approval immediately (Ben + Lauren).

I’ve attached the usage snapshot (same as you sent); also linking the HubSpot deal so we keep the record up to date.

Thanks — I can do the burst now if you say go.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
+1 (650) 555-0192

Attachment(s): usage_snapshot_20261103.csv
Related: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/CLW-2026-317
message_3_subject: FW: Urgent: Friday traffic spike — request for immediate uplift and credit (Clearway AI)
message_3_body:
Ben / Lauren — forwarding Clearway’s ask. TL;DR: 24h +3x uplift for Friday to avoid customer outage. Estimated overrun ~$4.2k at PAYG. They’re asking whether we can (a) do immediate uplift, and (b) consider a one-time goodwill credit for ~20% because this was an internal rollout issue.

My proposed operational path: apply option 1 (instant burst) now to stop throttling, then follow up with invoice smoothing for the billing impact. For the credit, I’m requesting discretion: offer a 10% immediate credit and propose a conditional retro credit up to 20% if they convert to a short-term reserved uplift (30–60 days) within 14 days. This gives us leverage to convert transient customers to a committed uplift.

Questions for you: 1) Approve 10% immediate credit (finance will do an adjusting memo), 2) If we want to push for conversion incentive (25% retro credit on overrun if they commit to 6 months), or keep the conditional 20% on a 30–60d uplift. Lauren — any legal or procurement wording to prepare (amendment template/DocuSign) if they accept conversion?

If you approve, I’ll apply burst now and tell them we’ll hold 10% credit pending official signoff.

Thanks — Jasmine

message_4_subject: Re: FW: Urgent: Friday traffic spike — request for immediate uplift and credit (Clearway AI)
message_4_body:
Jasmine — thanks for the quick rundown. Approve the immediate uplift and a customer-facing concession with limits. Specifics: 

- Approve 10% one-time credit against the overrun (cap $1,000) to be issued as an invoice adjustment. Finance to route the memo.
- Hold the conditional conversion incentive: offer a 25% retro rebate on this incident if Clearway signs a 6-month committed uplift minimum within 14 days. Sales to own the conversion terms; Legal (Lauren) please prepare a short amendment/DocuSign template and procurement language.
- Operationally apply the +3x capacity for 24 hours now. Charge PAYG for usage above commit, prorated. We’ll issue the credit after we receive their postmortem and confirm route IDs.

Grace — can you coordinate billing to prepare an adjusted invoice and a credit memo (10% cap $1k)? Finance will need the usage CSV and final meter read by EOD.

Jasmine — tell them ETA for uplift and confirm whether they want invoice smoothing. I’d avoid blanket forgiveness; this gives us a conversion path while being reasonable.

— Ben Carter
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
